whoIsThisFor.heading: Who is the Marketing Cloud Personalization exam for?

personas.label: Personalization specialists
personas.description: You set up real-time experiences across web and email with Marketing Cloud Personalization, formerly Interaction Studio, and want to validate that work.

personas.label: Marketing Cloud implementation partners
personas.description: You deliver Personalization implementations for customers and need to show hands-on platform knowledge.

personas.label: E-commerce and content strategists
personas.description: You manage product suggestions or dynamic content and want to demonstrate skills with Einstein Recipes and campaign targeting.

examDifficulty.heading: Is the Marketing Cloud Personalization Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: The exam covers how Personalization collects behavior and uses it for relevant experiences. Prepare for web SDK setup, catalog data, Einstein Recipes, campaign configuration, and experiment measurement. Prior implementation experience makes the scenarios easier to reason through.
bullets: 50 scored questions in 75 minutes, plus up to five unscored questions that do not count.
70% to pass, which is 35 correct answers out of 50.
Understand how the web SDK captures behavior and sends events to Personalization.
Review Einstein Recipe approaches and how strategies can use boosters and exclusions.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Get hands-on with the web SDK, a product catalog, and several campaigns. Configure an A/B test and try Einstein Recipes so you can connect each setting to an actual use case.

examFormat.heading: Marketing Cloud Personalization Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: The exam is proctored online or at a test center. Scenario questions may ask you to choose a campaign delivery method, build a recommendation strategy, or trigger an experience from segment membership.
examFormat.scenarioPercent: About 50–60% of questions are scenario-based. Be ready to choose a campaign delivery method, configure recommendations for a page, or respond to a visitor entering a segment.
bestWayToPass: Understand how the web beacon and sitemap identify page types, catalog items, and visitor actions. Know how those events reach the Personalization service.
Compare Collaborative Filtering, Content Affinity, and User Trending. Practice combining recipe output with strategy rules, boosters, and exclusions.
Review web campaigns, triggered email, open-time email, and server-side delivery. Choose based on when and where the experience must appear.
Set up a control group and review measures such as click-through rate and revenue per impression to assess campaign lift.

certificationCard.description: This exam covers Marketing Cloud Personalization setup, recommendations, campaigns, and testing. The certification details list 60 questions, a 75-minute limit, and a 70% passing score.

keyConcepts.h2: Marketing Cloud Personalization: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: Catalog and unified profiles
blocks.body: Personalization collects behavior across channels and builds a unified view of each visitor. Its catalog stores products, articles, and other recommendable items with attributes. Catalog records can arrive through a sitemap, feed, or API. The profile brings together engagement from web, email, mobile, and other connected touchpoints.

blocks.heading: Einstein Recipes and strategies
blocks.body: Recipes use different signals to select items. Collaborative Filtering finds items associated with behavior from similar users; Content Affinity reflects attributes a visitor tends to engage with; User Trending uses popularity signals. A strategy can combine recipes with rules, such as excluding previously viewed items, requiring stock, or boosting selected attributes. Choose a mix that fits the placement and goal.

blocks.heading: Web campaigns and delivery
blocks.body: Campaigns deliver personalized experiences. Server-side campaigns prepare content before the page is rendered and can avoid visible page changes. Client-side campaigns update the page after load and suit elements such as overlays or callouts. A/B tests compare a treatment experience with a control that continues to see the default.

blocks.heading: Segments and triggered experiences
blocks.body: Segments describe audiences using profile fields and behavior, such as category affinity or lifecycle stage. They can change as new activity arrives. A triggered campaign can respond when someone enters or leaves a segment or performs an action, such as viewing a product or abandoning a basket. Experiences can reach web, mobile, or connected email journeys.

blocks.heading: Email and Salesforce connections
blocks.body: Personalization can provide recommendations for Marketing Cloud email through supported integrations, including AMPscript or open-time email approaches. Journey Builder can use segment events to start journeys. Salesforce CRM connections can surface recommendations in Sales or Service Cloud. Measure outcomes such as revenue associated with recommendations, not only the number displayed.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Salesforce Marketing Cloud Personalization Accredited Professional Exam
scenarioTips.intro: This exam focuses on using behavior and profile data to tailor experiences in real time. Study SDK and sitemap setup, catalog quality, campaign design, and measurement.

blocks.heading: Web SDK Implementation
blocks.body: Learn how the Personalization web SDK is installed and how sitemap mappings describe pages, catalog items, and events.

blocks.heading: Catalog & User Profile
blocks.body: Review catalog item types and attributes, and how profile fields built from events support audience segments.

blocks.heading: Campaign Types
blocks.body: Compare in-page web campaigns, triggered email, open-time email, and server-side experiences; understand their Marketing Cloud connections.

blocks.heading: Einstein Recipes & Recommendations
blocks.body: Distinguish recipe approaches such as trending, recently viewed, similar items, and collaborative filtering. Learn how strategy boosters and exclusions shape results.

blocks.heading: Reporting & A/B Testing
blocks.body: Read reports using impressions, click-through rate, and revenue per impression. Use a control group to estimate the incremental effect.

nextCertsAfter.heading: Next Certifications After This AP
nextCertsAfter.intro: These Salesforce credentials complement an AP in personalization with platform and implementation knowledge.

sampleQuestions.question: A shop wants its homepage recommendations to respond to a visitor’s current activity. What signal is needed?
options: A manually curated list of products chosen by the merchandising team weekly
A segment built the previous week from the visitor's purchase history alone
A nightly batch job that recalculates the recommendations for every visitor
Behaviour evaluated in the current session
sampleQuestions.explanation: Current-session events let the experience adapt to what the visitor is viewing or doing now.
whyWrong: A hand-curated list is the same for everyone and never adapts.
Last week's segment misses everything about this visit.
A nightly batch cannot react to something that happened a minute ago.

sampleQuestions.question: What information is stored in a Marketing Cloud Personalization catalog?
options: The structured set of items that can be recommended
The list of email templates available for use in a personalized campaign
The record of every page each visitor has viewed over the last twelve months
The schedule controlling when each personalization campaign goes live
sampleQuestions.explanation: The catalog contains recommendable products or content and the attributes used to describe them.
whyWrong: Email templates are content assets, not catalog items.
Visitor history is behavioural data rather than the catalog.
Campaign scheduling is a separate configuration.

sampleQuestions.question: Why do complete, accurate catalog attributes improve recommendations?
options: The number of attributes decides how many campaigns can run at one time
Recommendations can only use attributes that exist
Attributes determine how quickly each web page will load for the visitor
Attributes are required before any email can be sent to a known visitor
sampleQuestions.explanation: Strategies can only filter and rank using available attributes, so gaps or inconsistent values limit relevance.
whyWrong: Campaign capacity is not a function of attribute count.
Attribute data does not drive page load performance.
Email sending does not depend on catalog attributes.

sampleQuestions.question: A visitor browses before signing in. How can Personalization use that earlier activity?
options: The session is tied to their known profile
The known profile is replaced entirely by the new anonymous session data
The anonymous activity is discarded as soon as they authenticate themselves
Two separate profiles are kept permanently, one anonymous and one known
sampleQuestions.explanation: Identity resolution can connect the anonymous activity to the known visitor profile after sign-in.
whyWrong: Overwriting the known profile would destroy its history.
Discarding pre-login behaviour throws away the most recent intent signal.
Leaving the profiles separate means neither view is complete.

sampleQuestions.question: What does a visitor’s affinity score describe?
options: The total amount of money the visitor has spent across all their orders
How strongly a visitor leans towards an attribute
The position a product occupies in the merchandising team's priority list
The number of separate sessions the visitor has started in a given month
sampleQuestions.explanation: An affinity score reflects the visitor’s observed preference for a category, brand, or other attribute.
whyWrong: Lifetime spend is a monetary measure, not an affinity.
Merchandising priority is a business decision, not visitor behaviour.
Session count measures frequency of visits.

sampleQuestions.question: How can a campaign target visitors who added an item to the basket but did not buy?
options: As a segment based on in-session behaviour
As a change to the catalog attributes on each of the products in the basket
As a nightly export of abandoned baskets sent to the email platform instead
As a manual list of visitors compiled each morning by the marketing team
sampleQuestions.explanation: Define a behavior-based segment for visitors who added an item and have not completed checkout.
whyWrong: Catalog attributes describe items, not visitor state.
A nightly export cannot drive an on-site message during the visit.
A manual list cannot keep pace with live sessions.

sampleQuestions.question: What does the control group tell you in a campaign experiment?
options: To ensure that each visitor sees the campaign no more than once per session
To show what would have happened without it
To reduce the amount of traffic the personalization engine has to process
To satisfy a requirement that every campaign is reviewed before it goes live
sampleQuestions.explanation: A control group provides a baseline, helping distinguish campaign lift from changes that would have happened anyway.
whyWrong: Frequency capping is a separate campaign setting.
Control groups are about measurement, not reducing load.
Review processes are unrelated to holdout measurement.

sampleQuestions.question: How does an Einstein Recipe differ from a single recommendation rule?
options: A recipe runs overnight whereas a simple rule is evaluated in real time
A recipe applies to email while a simple rule applies only to the website
A recipe is configured by a developer and a rule by a marketing user
A recipe combines and weights several strategies
sampleQuestions.explanation: A recipe can combine recommendation approaches and weight their contributions; a simple rule applies a condition or sort.
whyWrong: Recipes are evaluated in real time as well.
Both can serve web and email channels.
Either can be configured without development work.

sampleQuestions.question: What should a strategy do when purchased items should no longer be recommended?
options: A reduction in the total number of recommendations shown on the page
A nightly refresh of the affinity scores held against each visitor profile
A new catalog containing only the items that have never been purchased
An exclusion rule for purchased items
sampleQuestions.explanation: Add an exclusion based on purchase history so previously bought items are removed from the results.
whyWrong: Showing fewer bad recommendations does not make them relevant.
Refreshing affinity does not stop already-purchased items appearing.
A separate catalog per visitor is unworkable.

sampleQuestions.question: What does the Personalization sitemap or tracking setup describe to the platform?
options: It lists the URLs that search engines are permitted to index on the site
It tells the platform what each page and action means
It records which marketing emails each visitor has opened and clicked
It controls which pages are cached by the content delivery network used
sampleQuestions.explanation: The setup maps pages, items, and visitor actions so Personalization can interpret incoming activity.
whyWrong: Search engine indexing is handled by a different kind of sitemap.
Email engagement is tracked by the email platform.
Caching is a delivery concern.

sampleQuestions.question: Why can personalized search results be useful alongside product recommendations?
options: Search results are the only part of a website that can be personalized
Personalising search removes the need to maintain catalog attributes
Search already signals strong intent
Search traffic is unaffected by the visitor's own browsing behaviour
sampleQuestions.explanation: A search query signals immediate intent, and visitor context can help rank matching results more usefully.
whyWrong: Most of the page can be personalized, not just search.
Search personalization depends on catalog attributes rather than replacing them.
Browsing behaviour is highly relevant to how results should be ranked.

sampleQuestions.question: Desktop results are strong, but mobile results are weak. What should the team do?
options: Apply the desktop version unchanged and wait for the figures to improve
Switch the campaign off entirely across both of the available channels
Treat them as separate contexts and adjust
Assume the mobile measurement is wrong and continue without any change
sampleQuestions.explanation: Review mobile placement and behavior separately, then adjust the campaign for that device context.
whyWrong: Waiting for an unchanged campaign to improve is not a plan.
Turning off a campaign that works on desktop discards real value.
Dismissing inconvenient data is not a response.

sampleQuestions.question: What does a campaign frequency cap limit?
options: It limits how often a visitor sees the message
It caps the number of separate campaigns that may run on a single page
It restricts the number of catalog items that may appear in each placement
It sets a maximum number of visitors who can be shown the campaign at once
sampleQuestions.explanation: A frequency cap sets the maximum number of times the same visitor sees a campaign.
whyWrong: Campaign conflicts are handled by prioritisation.
Item count per placement is a separate setting.
Audience size is governed by the segment, not a frequency cap.

sampleQuestions.question: Which evidence best shows the financial effect of personalization?
options: The volume of behavioural events the platform captured across the website
The number of campaigns the marketing team managed to launch that quarter
Conversion and revenue against the control group
The total number of personalized impressions served during the period
sampleQuestions.explanation: Compare conversion and revenue for the treatment against the control to estimate incremental value.
whyWrong: Event volume shows the platform is working, not that it earns money.
Campaign count measures team output rather than outcome.
Impression volume is activity, not value.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the central purpose of Marketing Cloud Personalization?
options: Manages the paid advertising budget across each of the available channels
Sends scheduled marketing emails to segments built the previous evening
Decides what each visitor sees, as they browse
Stores the organisation's consolidated customer records across every system
sampleQuestions.explanation: It uses visitor profile and current behavior to choose a relevant experience in the moment.
whyWrong: Paid media budgeting is handled by advertising tools.
Scheduled email sending is Marketing Cloud Engagement's role.
Consolidated customer records sit in Data Cloud.
